contentFindings.where: pH scale: PH_EXAMPLES and genPH EX
contentFindings.issue: "4% sodium hydroxide" is placed at pH 13. 4% NaOH is about 1.0 M (41 g/L), so pH ≈ 14; the page itself pairs 4% HCl with 1 M HCl at pH 0.
contentFindings.fix: Label pH 13 as "0.4% (0.1 M) sodium hydroxide", or move 4% NaOH to pH 14.

contentFindings.issue: Lead 0.015 mg/L and copper 1.3 mg/L are action levels under the Lead and Copper Rule, not maximum contaminant levels (lead MCLG is zero); the 2024 LCRI lowers the lead action level to 0.010 mg/L.
contentFindings.fix: Call them "action levels" and note the 0.010 mg/L update.

contentFindings.issue: Two different elements with equal electronegativity (C–S, P–H, N–Cl, C–I, S–I) are drawn with δ+ and δ− labels while the text says ΔEN = 0.0, nonpolar.
contentFindings.fix: Only draw δ labels when d > 0.4 (or at least when d > 0).

contentFindings.issue: With the course values H–I gives ΔEN 0.4 → "nonpolar covalent"; with current Pauling values (2.20, 2.66) ΔEN = 0.46 → polar, and HI has a measurable dipole (0.44 D).
contentFindings.fix: Drop H–I from BOND_PAIRS or accept it as a borderline case.

contentFindings.issue: Blue litmus is said to turn red for any pH below 6.95 (e.g. 6.9). Litmus changes over roughly pH 4.5–8.3, so near-neutral solutions give no clear change.
contentFindings.fix: Say "turns red in clearly acidic solutions (below about 5)".

contentFindings.issue: "about four times that of rock or metal": water 4.18 vs iron 0.449 (9×), copper 0.385 (11×), rock ≈0.8 (5×).
contentFindings.fix: "5 to 10 times".

contentFindings.where: Solutions note, key term "Hard water"; EPA iron note
contentFindings.issue: Hardness is defined by Ca2+ and Mg2+; iron is not usually counted as a hardness ion.
contentFindings.fix: Drop iron from the hardness definition.

contentFindings.issue: "about 0.7–1.0 ppm" — the U.S. PHS recommendation since 2015 is 0.7 mg/L.
contentFindings.fix: "about 0.7 ppm".

contentFindings.issue: At pH 6.9 or 7.1 the text says "about 1 times more/less" hydrogen ion (10^0.1 = 1.26 rounded to 0 decimals). "10−0" appears for pH 0 and 14.
contentFindings.fix: Use 2 significant figures; write pH 0 as "1 mol/L".

contentFindings.where: Fossil fuels: MAPINFO, lede, review quiz (answer "More than 90%"), key term
contentFindings.issue: Fossil fuels supplied nearly 83% of U.S. energy in 2023 (EIA), about 80% worldwide, not "more than 90%". The review quiz marks "More than 90%" correct.
contentFindings.fix: Use "about 80%" and change the quiz key.

contentFindings.where: Radiation: ideas text, review quiz, key term "Background radiation"
contentFindings.issue: "About three-fourths ... is natural background" and "CT scans alone are about a quarter" contradict the page’s own Figure 11.1 data (NCRP 160: background 50%, medical 48%). The review quiz keys "Three-fourths".
contentFindings.fix: Say "about half" (NCRP 160) and re-key the quiz.

contentFindings.issue: "Marie Curie isolated radium in 1898": radium was discovered in 1898; it was isolated as RaCl2 in 1902 and as the metal in 1910.
contentFindings.fix: "discovered radium in 1898".

contentFindings.issue: Beta "can penetrate a few centimeters of skin and tissue": typical ranges are a few millimetres (about 1 cm at most for energetic betas).
contentFindings.fix: "a few millimetres of tissue".

contentFindings.issue: "Launched in 1939": the 1939 Einstein–Szilárd letter led to the Uranium Committee; the Manhattan Project (Manhattan Engineer District) began in 1942.
contentFindings.fix: "Begun in 1942, after physicists warned Roosevelt in 1939".

contentFindings.issue: The "2017" values (gas 33.8, coal 30.4, nuclear 19.7, hydro 6.5, wind 5.5) are EIA 2016 figures; EIA gives gas 32% and coal 30% for 2017. The "2003" values (coal 45, gas 23, petroleum 1) look like about 2009; in 2003 coal was about half. Both are a decade old (2024: gas ≈43%, coal ≈15%).
contentFindings.fix: Relabel or update from EIA Electric Power Annual.

contentFindings.where: Reactor fuel 2.5–3.5% U-235 (several places); US 104 plants; France 73%
contentFindings.issue: Current LWR fuel is about 3–5% U-235; the U.S. has 94 reactors; France ≈65% in 2023.
contentFindings.fix: Update or add "(2012 data)".

contentFindings.issue: Sodium-24 half-life listed 14.66 h; NNDC gives 14.96 h. Other older textbook values: Pu-238 86 y (87.7), Sr-90 28.5 y (28.8), H-3 12.26 y (12.32), U-238 4.51 (4.47) billion y.
contentFindings.fix: 14.96 h; optionally update the others.

contentFindings.issue: "Iron has the most tightly bound nucleus" (Ni-62 has the highest binding energy per nucleon); "every element heavier than uranium exists only because of artificial transmutation" (trace Np and Pu occur naturally).
contentFindings.fix: "iron and nickel"; "nearly all".

contentFindings.issue: "In the breaker lab, a 1:1 bottom gives an Iribarren number far into the plunging range": ξ0 = 1/√(H0/L0) ≈ 11–12 for H0 2–4 m, T 14–18 s, which is "surging" (> 3.3) by the page’s own table; even the 1:3 slope gives 3.7–4.2. The lab’s steepest slope is 1:5, so it cannot be tried.
contentFindings.fix: Say the Iribarren classes were fitted for plane beaches; a reef that rises abruptly from deep water is outside that range and plunges anyway.

contentFindings.issue: Daytona Beach "averages about 68 °F in winter", "high 60s" in winter: monthly means are about 65 °F in January–February (61–69 °F range), 68 °F is the December mean; NOAA’s nearshore guide lists cooler.
contentFindings.fix: "low to mid 60s °F in January–February".

contentFindings.issue: Fetch-limited fits are the SPM constants (0.0016, 0.286) but the fully developed cap uses 0.21 and 7.7; at 30 mph the peak period jumps 10.0 → 10.5 s (5%) between 190 and 200 mi of fetch.
contentFindings.fix: Use one set: SPM fully developed gH/U² = 0.2433 and gT/U = 8.134 make both curves continuous.

contentFindings.issue: Butyl rubber is the isobutylene–isoprene copolymer (IIR); PIB homopolymer cannot be sulfur-vulcanized.
contentFindings.fix: "Polyisobutylene (with ~2% isoprene: butyl rubber)".

contentFindings.issue: Drawn as the trans (fumarate) C=C although the monomer shown is maleic anhydride (cis). Correct for the cured resin (maleate isomerizes during polyesterification) but unexplained.
contentFindings.fix: Add "(the cis maleate isomerizes to trans fumarate as it polymerizes)".

contentFindings.issue: "Ponce and New Smyrna inlets": Ponce de León Inlet is the inlet at New Smyrna Beach; they are one inlet.
contentFindings.fix: "Ponce Inlet (New Smyrna Beach)".

contentFindings.issue: The ethylene SVG renders 31 × 4 px and looks like a minus sign (bare double bond, no atom labels). PVAc’s subscript n overlaps the acetate oxygen.
contentFindings.fix: Draw H2C=CH2 with explicit carbons; nudge n.

contentFindings.issue: Submerged volume uses only the "Rider + gear mass" slider; the board’s own mass is left out unless counted as gear (practice problem 9 adds it).
contentFindings.fix: Label "Rider + board + gear".
